 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the 2nd respondent insurance company challenging the liability to pay the compensation awarded by the tribunal in O.P (MV) No.1266 of 2009 of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Pathanamthitta.
The respondents herein are the petitioners and 1st respondent before the tribunal.

2. The case of the claimant before the tribunal is that on 04.10.2009, while the deceased was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KL-24-A-729 owned by the first respondent, an unidentified vehicle came from the opposite direction without dimming its head light.
Due to the negligent act of the driver, the deceased lost control, sustained serious injuries and ultimately succumbed to the injuries.
The legal heirs approached the tribunal claiming compensation.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner of the motorcycle and the 2nd respondent is the insurer.
The 1 st and 2nd respondents have filed written statements.

The 2nd respondent filed a written statement The Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Sreelekha S on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170763216/

sentences.text: contending that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the deceased who drove the motorcycle and admitted the policy coverage for the vehicle, but disputing the quantum of compensation claimed.
Before the tribunal, Exts.A1 to A6 were marked.

The 2025:KER:50074 MACA NO. 2889 OF 2014 tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record awarded a sum of 4,36,167/- as compensation under different heads with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of petition till realization, against the second respondent being the insurer.
Challenging the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal, the insurer has come up in appeal.

4. Heard the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the appellant/insurance company and the learned counsel appearing for the respondents/claimants.
5.
The learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that the accident occurred on 04.10.2009 at 07.30p.m., and it was a self accident.
The deceased was the rider of the motorcycle and hit an electric post and sustained injuries due to which he succumbed to the injuries on the same day.
The claim petition was filed under Section 163 A of the Motor Vehicles Act.

It is further submitted that there was no offending vehicle and the rider of the vehicle will step into the shoes of the owner; hence, he is not entitled to claim any amount from his own insurance company.
Since it is a self-accident, the insurance company cannot be held liable to pay the compensation.

6. The learned counsel appearing for the claimant, however, 2025:KER:50074 MACA NO. 2889 OF 2014 submitted that in the present case, the accident occurred when an unidentified vehicle, coming from the opposite direction without dimming its headlight, caused the deceased to lose control of the motorcycle and collided with an electric post.
Hence, this cannot be considered a case of self-accident.
7. I have considered the rival contentions raised by both sides.
8. On a perusal of the documents and the facts narrated in the award, it is seen that the accident occurred due to the hit of the motorcycle on an electric post.
The learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that the charge was against the rider of the motorcycle.
However, in a petition filed under 163A, there is no necessity to prove negligence on the part of the rider.

Since, it is said that it was a self accident and the claim was under 163A, the learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance company relied on the policy issued and submitted that they are not liable to compensate the claimants for the death occurred due to the injuries sustained in the accident.

However, though the appeal is filed solely on the basis of the insurance policy, the insurance company failed to produce a copy of the policy either before the Tribunal or before this Court in appeal.

The learned counsel appearing for the claimant, however, submits that it is not clear as to the terms of the policy, since 2025:KER:50074 MACA NO. 2889 OF 2014 the copy of the policy is not available.
I find force in the said submission of the learned counsel for the respondent.
However, the standing counsel appearing for the insurer seeks for one more opportunity to prove their contentions.
In order to meet the ends of justice, I find that one more opportunity is to be granted to the insurance company to prove their contentions before the tribunal.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the appeal is disposed of as follows:
The award dated 05.06.2014 in O.P (MV) No.1266 of 2009 is hereby set aside.

The tribunal is directed to re-consider the entire issue on merits in accordance with law,
after affording opportunity to both sides to adduce fresh evidence.
The parties are also free to produce any document, if so required, before the tribunal to prove their contentions.
In the absence of the insurer producing the policy or any evidence to substantiate their contentions, after granting sufficient time, the original award passed by the tribunal shall stand.

The learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that pursuant to the interim order of this Court in the appeal, the appellant insurer has deposited an amount of rupees two lakhs before the tribunal and the said amount was got released by the claimants in this case.
However, it is made clear that the tribunal shall look into the afore aspect, while deciding the appeal on merits.
The parties are directed to appear before the tribunal on 18.08.2025.

Sd/-
